privacyAssessment.dataSubjectRights: not-applicable — `source` records which platform mechanism raised a backlog item. It describes no person and is never derived from one.
privacyAssessment.reviewDisposition: No data-subject workflow is introduced or changed. The change widens the set of values a column may hold; it neither reads, writes, nor reclassifies any personal data.

migration.name: 20260922120000_backlog_source_allows_data_growth
migration.backfill: None required, and none possible to need. The constraint is widened, never narrowed, so no existing row can violate it: every value currently stored was already permitted by the previous set, which is a strict subset of the new one. DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS then ADD makes the statement idempotent, so replaying it against a database that already has the widened form is a no-op. NOT VALID matches the sibling constraints from 20260816111000_closed_set_check_expand and skips the full-table re-check, which is safe here for the same reason: there is nothing for it to find.
migration.rollback: Forward-only by convention, but trivially reversible: a corrective migration re-adds the constraint without 'data-growth'. That would only be correct if the writer were also removed, because narrowing it again is what caused this defect — the writer would resume failing silently.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: BacklogItem is a retained work record and stays one. No row is created, altered, deleted or re-identified by this change. What changes is the set of values one existing TEXT column may accept, so that an existing writer's existing value stops being rejected at insert time.

fields.reason: The permitted set gains 'data-growth', the value captureCorrectiveFailureBI has sent since EP-A33A5C61 slice 5 shipped. Until now every such insert failed with Postgres 23514 and was swallowed by that function's deliberate best-effort catch, so the table-growth steward detected persistent findings for eleven consecutive nights and filed none of them (BI-4C6934CF). Widening the set is what makes the steward's filing path real; the column type, its nullability and every stored value are untouched.
fields.provenance: BI-4C6934CF; portal log shows four 23514 rejections per night; verified on the live install by an INSERT with source='data-growth' inside a transaction that was rolled back, which the widened constraint accepted.
